n: Nephi senses his readers wondering what to do next after entering the gate. He gently asks why they are puzzled—he has already given the answer.
He reminds them: after receiving the Holy Ghost they can speak with the “tongue of angels”—which is only possible through the Holy Ghost.
Angels speak Christ’s words by the Holy Ghost. So feast on Christ’s words—through scripture and the Spirit—and they will tell you everything you need to do.

f.w: feast upon the words of Christ
tell you all things what ye should do

n: If anyone still doesn’t understand, it’s because they haven’t asked or knocked. Light is available but must be sought.

f.w: ask not, neither do ye knock

n: Nephi repeats: enter by the gate, receive the Holy Ghost, and it will show you all things you should do.

f.w: it will show unto you all things

n: This is the doctrine of Christ; no more will be given until Christ appears in the flesh among them—which happened in 3 Nephi—and then they must obey what he says.

f.w: manifest himself unto you in the flesh

n: The Spirit stops Nephi from saying more. He mourns that people will not seek or accept knowledge even when it is taught as plainly as possible.

f.g: Stubborn refusal to bend or be taught.

n: Nephi grieves that some still hesitate. The Spirit teaches us to pray; the evil spirit teaches us not to. That alone shows which influence to follow.

f.w: the evil spirit teacheth not a man to pray

n: Pray always and don’t give up. Before doing anything for the Lord, pray that the Father will consecrate it—make it holy and beneficial for your soul.
